UTI treatment with a pharmacist at Pacific Fair

Yes, women aged 18 to 65 can be assessed and, if suitable, treated for an uncomplicated urinary tract infection by a trained pharmacist at Priceline Pharmacy Pacific Fair in Broadbeach, without a GP visit. The consultation takes about 15 minutes in our private room; a fee applies and isn’t covered by Medicare. No booking is needed, so walk in and ask for a trained pharmacist.

Call (07) 5592 2099 Hours & directions

At a glance

A private assessment by a trained pharmacist who can supply treatment for an uncomplicated urinary tract infection if suitable.
Who it's for
Women aged 18 to 65 with symptoms of an uncomplicated bladder infection.

Who can use the pharmacy UTI service?

The Queensland pharmacy UTI service is for women aged 18 to 65 with symptoms of an uncomplicated bladder infection (cystitis), such as:

  • burning or stinging when you pass urine
  • needing to go more often, or urgently
  • discomfort low in your tummy

What happens in the consultation?

  1. Your pharmacist asks about your symptoms, health history and any medicines you take, in private.
  2. If the service is suitable for you, the pharmacist can supply a treatment and explain how to take it.
  3. If it isn’t suitable, we’ll refer you to a GP. Help Medical is an independent general practice located inside our store.

Allow about 15 minutes.

How much does it cost?

A consultation fee applies and isn’t covered by Medicare. Ask us about the fee when you call on (07) 5592 2099.

When do I need to see a GP instead?

Pharmacists can’t treat UTIs through this service if you:

  • are pregnant, or might be
  • are under 18 or over 65
  • are male
  • have frequent or recurring UTIs
  • have kidney problems, a urinary catheter or a weakened immune system

When should I get urgent medical help?

Get medical help the same day if you have:

  • a fever, chills or shaking
  • pain in your back or side
  • blood in your urine
  • nausea or vomiting

These can be signs the infection has spread to your kidneys. See a GP the same day, or go to an emergency department. In an emergency, call 000.

What can I do to feel better in the meantime?

  • Drink plenty of water, especially in Gold Coast heat.
  • Don’t hold on when you need to go.
  • Ask our pharmacists about products to ease discomfort while you wait for treatment to work.

Always read the label and follow the directions for use. For other support, see our women’s health page.

Common questions

Do I need to book?

No. Walk in and ask for a trained pharmacist at the prescription counter. If you’re travelling a long way, you’re welcome to call ahead to check how busy we are.

Do I need a prescription?

No. If the service is suitable for you, the trained pharmacist supplies the treatment directly, without a GP visit. Walk in and ask at the prescription counter.

Can men use this service?

No. The Queensland pharmacy UTI service is for women aged 18 to 65. Men with UTI symptoms should see a GP; Help Medical is inside our store.

Can I use the service if I’m pregnant?

No. If you’re pregnant, or might be, you’ll need to see a GP, because UTIs in pregnancy need different care. Help Medical, inside our store, can see you.

Is the consultation covered by Medicare?

No. A consultation fee applies and isn’t covered by Medicare. Call us and ask about the fee before you come in.

What if my symptoms don’t improve?

If your symptoms get worse, or haven’t improved after a few days, see a GP. If you develop a fever, back pain, blood in your urine or vomiting, get medical help the same day.
